# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**Member:** Cameron Carter
**Member ID:** W300143742
**Plan:** UnitedHealthcare / Oxford (Commercial/ACA), New Jersey
**Denial date:** 2026-08-16
**Reference number:** POC-3469ABE4FC-29435
**Governing policy:** Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O) — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-ankle.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which was denied on 2026-08-16 as not medically necessary. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is needed for my condition, and I believe the records support that under the plan's own policy.

## The plan's general coverage rule

The policy states:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

My records show why my case falls within those circumstances. I have had 9 months of progressive ankle pain that did not improve with rest. I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, 2026-03-13 through 2026-07-03), which is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I used NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-14 gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. Weight-bearing ankle radiographs on 2026-06-28 showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. I currently walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks, and my exam showed positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion. I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. These are the kinds of findings — a joint that has failed extended conservative treatment and shows structural damage on imaging — that the circumstances described in the plan's own coverage rationale are meant to address.

## The InterQual criteria referenced by the plan

The policy also states:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:"

and lists:

> "Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint) Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle Arthrotomy, Ankle Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

The denial notice does not tell me which specific InterQual subset or edition was applied to my case, or which specific criteria within it my records allegedly failed to meet. Without that text, I cannot fully respond to the basis for the denial, and I am requesting it below.

## The osteochondral allograft/autograft criteria do not appear to apply

The policy also contains language stating:

> "Osteochondral allograft or autograft transplant is unproven and not medically necessary for treating cartilage defects of the ankle due to insufficient evidence of efficacy."

and cites supporting language that:

> "All studies exhibited a high risk of bias in at least one domain, with 64% demonstrating a high risk across at least four domains."

and that:

> "however, a considerable number of the allografts failed, requiring repeat allografting, arthrodesis, or arthroplasty (range, 11%-48%)."

The procedure my surgeon requested is a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), not an osteochondral allograft or autograft transplant for a cartilage defect. My imaging findings describe joint space obliteration and subchondral cysts, not a focal osteochondral lesion. I ask the plan to clarify whether this allograft/autograft language was applied to my case in error, since it does not appear to describe the procedure requested or the condition documented in my records.

## Documentation submitted

The policy notes:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

My surgeon's office has submitted physical therapy records, medication and injection history, imaging, and exam findings supporting this request. I am asking that these records be reviewed against the specific InterQual criteria for Ankle Total Joint Replacement referenced in the policy.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

The plan's policy states that it "may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits." Because InterQual is licensed software and not something I can access on my own, I am formally requesting, in writing and free of charge, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, along with an explanation of which specific criteria my records were found not to meet. I understand this request falls under my appeal rights under ERISA and ACA appeal regulations.

## What I am asking for

I am asking the plan to reconsider and approve coverage for CPT 27702, total ankle replacement, based on the records described above and the plan's own coverage rationale. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-12, and I am submitting it through my online account at member.uhc.com and/or by calling the number on my member ID card, consistent with the instructions on my denial notice.

Please contact me if any additional information is needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Carter**
Member ID: W300143742
[Address]

evidence.submission_route: Sign in at member.uhc.com and file the appeal there, or call the number on your card. There is no single public appeals fax or PO box — use the address on your denial letter. Online: member.uhc.com By phone: The number on your ID card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Your plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a public document. You have a right to it anyway: federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to give you, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on for the denial. Ask in writing for 'the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination'.
